transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-03-14
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Alex Mercer, Samira Khan, Rafael Ortiz (Redwood) — Priya Malhotra, Jonas Eriksson, Marco Reyes, Li Wei, Anya Petrov (NebulaCloud)
Shared artifacts: partnership one-pager (link: https://redwood.internal/papers/nebu-partner-onepager), integration-spec draft (to be shared), perf spreadsheet (link: https://sheets.example.com/redwood-nebula-benchmarks)

Optional auto sections:
Summary: Introductory partner discovery between Redwood Inference and NebulaCloud Systems to explore a joint integration for GPU instance qualification and a potential PoC to surface Redwood as a preferred inference runtime on NebulaCloud marketplace. High-level alignment around performance benchmarking, network/VPC connectivity, and compliance checks. Agreed next steps include sharing integration spec, Nebula providing instance SKUs and traces, and scheduling PoC scoping.
Topics: partner go-to-market, GPU SKUs and drivers, private deployments (VPC), latency/cost tradeoffs, benchmarking methodology, compliance matrix, PoC scope
Action items: See metadata field below

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time — appreciate it. Can folks quick-introduce themselves so we have context?
[00:12] Priya (NebulaCloud): Sure, I'm Priya, head of partnerships at NebulaCloud, we run the cloud plus a marketplace and we're trying to figure out LLM inference partnerships. Jonas is our GPU integration lead, Marco is the cloud arc person, and Li handles compliance. Anya is business dev.
[00:27] Alex: Great, Alex here — I run partnerships at Redwood. Samira is our systems SE, Rafael is on solutions. Quick note: goal for today is to understand Nebula's priorities (marketplace, target customers), their GPU stack, and what a first PoC would look like.
[00:45] Jonas (NebulaCloud): Quick housekeeping, this call is recorded and we'll share notes. We have a mix of customers — enterprise SaaS, adtech, and some research groups. Main ask: lowest latency and predictable cost on our infra, and we want Redwood as a well-integrated runtime.
[01:10] Samira (Redwood SE): Awesome. Can you lay out the actual GPU SKUs you run? Is it A100, H100, custom Ampere clones, or mixes? And do you expose PCI passthrough or MIG?
[01:28] Jonas: We're running a mix. Majority is A100 40GB and H100 in our newest zones. We also have a smaller fleet of 80GB A100s for high-memory jobs. We support MIG on some nodes but not universally, and for now customers get VM-like instances with curated drivers.
[01:50] Marco (NebulaCloud): For marketplace integrations we can offer pre-baked images with drivers, and we can set up private endpoints (VPC peering or private links) — depends on the customer's networking.
[02:06] Samira: Good. Any constraints on kernel versions, or do you allow us to ship a container with specific kernels? Sometimes quantized runtimes want specific libc/driver combos.
[02:22] Marco: We lock drivers at the host level, but you can bring containers. We do have an image build process where we can bake recommended drivers into the image if the partner needs that.
[02:36] Priya: From a GTM standpoint, we care about a clean integration story — a marketplace tile, quick onboarding, and co-marketing. Also procurement alignment for enterprise customers.
[02:50] Alex: Totally. From Redwood's side, we want to validate latency SLOs, demonstrate cost-per-token improvements with our batching and KV caching, and ensure the deployment patterns (hosted vs dedicated vs private) map to Nebula's SKU and network models.
[03:12] Jonas: On latency — what kind of numbers do you publish? And do you have automated benchmarking?
[03:20] Samira: We publish perf profiles per model/seq-length on our catalog, but for partner validation we'd run in-house microbenchmarks and a PoC harness. Rough numbers: on H100 with optimized kernels for quantized 8-bit, we often see 20-40% lower tail latency for typical chat workloads versus naive baseline. But that depends on batch sizes and prefix caching.
[03:45] Li (NebulaCloud): Related compliance question — does Redwood need customer data in the console? Are you storing any customer prompts or transcripts by default?
[03:57] Rafael (Redwood): Good Q. For private deployments and Dedicated, we support no-personal-data modes and can integrate with customer KMS/HSM. Hosted customers opt-in to logging; otherwise logs are redacted. We'll send our SOC2 and ISO artifact matrix.
[04:15] Li: Okay, we'll want the matrix and an overview of where data at rest and in transit is encrypted, key rotations etc.
[04:24] Samira: Noted. We'll include that in the security pack.
[04:29] Anya (NebulaCloud): On business terms — how do you typically structure partner revenue? Rev share on marketplace usage or referral fees?
[04:39] Alex: Often a joint model — marketplace listing with a rev share for marketplace-billed usage, or separate dedicated reserved capacity contracts for large customers. We can be flexible. We'll pass a partner economics one-pager after the call.
[04:55] Jonas: For the PoC scoping — we want to validate both throughput for batched inference (embedding pipelines) and latency for streaming chat. Can you support both in the same runtime?
[05:08] Samira: Yes, our runtime supports both continuous batching for throughput and low-latency single-request paths. There are knobs: you can trade off batching/windowing and get different tail-latency profiles.
[05:22] Marco: Networking — to hit low tail latencies, customers may want a VPC-private deployment in the same AZ as their app. Can Redwood run in Nebula's VPC or do you require outbound to your control plane?
[05:36] Rafael: For Redwood Private, control plane can be customer-managed; we can do a private control plane in VPC or on-prem. For the initial PoC we can run a lightweight private deployment with a direct peering.
[05:50] Priya: What about driver mismatches and CUDA versions — this is the painful part for our SREs.
[05:58] Samira: We'll produce a compatibility matrix as part of the integration spec, listing tested driver/CUDA/cuDNN combos. Ideally we test on your exact images.
[06:10] Jonas: Great. For metrics, we need percentile latencies, GPU utilization, memory footprint, and cost-per-token. We can expose Prometheus or push metrics to your system?
[06:22] Samira: We emit Prometheus-compatible metrics and can forward to a pushgateway. We also provide token-level cost breakdowns in the console for per-request accounting.
[06:35] Li: Another compliance follow-up — do you support customer-managed KMS for encryption of model artifacts? Some of our enterprise customers demand that keys never leave their HSM.
[06:46] Rafael: Yes, for Private deployments and Dedicated we support external KMS/HSM. We'll include integration notes for AWS KMS, HashiCorp Vault, and common HSMs.
[06:58] Anya: Any previous partner integrations on GPU marketplaces we should reference?
[07:05] Alex: We piloted with a couple of niche cloud partners last year — had a good reference for inference economics, happy to share anonymized case study numbers.
[07:15] Priya: For marketplace tile UX, can the image include a 'one-click' deploy of Redwood with pre-baked model versions?
[07:24] Rafael: Yes, we can produce a deployable image and a small operator chart that spins up the runtime + default model weights. For weight distribution we can integrate with Nebula's blobstore for model hosting or bring-your-own.
[07:38] Jonas: We have a question on model licensing — some customers want to use proprietary LLMs they'd bring to the runtime; do you support registering customer models?
[07:49] Samira: Yes, customers can bring their own models; Redwood supports pinning model versions and registering private artifacts. We need to verify format (HF, GGML, ONNX variants) — we'll add specifics to the spec.
[08:02] Marco: On resource isolation — can Redwood restrict GPU memory usage per tenant? For multi-tenant marketplace tiles we need strong isolation.
[08:14] Samira: We can do per-tenant scheduling and there are features like GPU partitioning (MIG) where possible. For strict isolation we recommend dedicated nodes per tenant.
[08:27] Priya: From a timeline standpoint, if we wanted a marketplace preview in Q2, what's realistic?
[08:35] Alex: For a minimal PoC and a marketplace tile preview, two to six weeks depending on availability of SKUs and traces. If we do full enterprise-ready private deployment with compliance sign-off, probably 8-12 weeks.
[08:50] Jonas: Ok we'll gather SKUs and customer priorities and share. Do you have a standard PoC checklist?
[08:58] Samira: Yes — we'll send a PoC checklist and runbook (network, images, metrics, SLAs) and propose a minimal test matrix: embedding throughput (batch sizes 64/128), streaming chat latency (seq len 512, 1-2 turn convo), and memory/VRAM residency.
[09:18] Li: Security — can we run a short threat model/architecture review during the PoC?
[09:24] Rafael: Absolutely. We can include a security review session and share our architecture diagram.
[09:30] Anya: On revenue ops, if we do rev share, how does billing work? Marketplace billing or direct billing?
[09:37] Alex: Both are possible — marketplace-billed usage simplifies revenue split; direct billing with invoicing works for large enterprise deals. We'll map options in the partner doc.
[09:48] Priya: Let's go into some technical specifics — Jonas, do you want to show the current perf we captured? (Jonas shares a short screen chart)
[10:00] Jonas: I pulled a 24-hour trace of production for one of our customers — embedding pipeline spikes at 3am UTC due to batch jobs. Tail latencies for single requests are spiky at 99th — around 700ms on A100 for that workload. We're hoping Redwood's caching/batching can reduce that.
[10:25] Samira: That sounds like prefix caching could help a lot if the workload has repeat prefixes. Also smarter batching during spikes can keep tail latency down while maintaining throughput. We'll need the request traces and ideally a sample corpus.
[10:40] Marco: We'll attach a link to a sanitized trace.
[10:45] Priya: Any blockers you foresee on the Redwood side to running on Nebula infra?
[10:51] Rafael: Nothing major; driver compatibility and kernel versions are the main friction points. Also, if the marketplace requires a signed image, we may need to coordinate signing keys.
[11:03] Alex: Quick note — competitors were mentioned: Lambda Labs and Paperspace; just to underscore, our differentiation is unified runtime across Hosted/Dedicated/Private and deep observability for cost/perf.
[11:19] Anya: Okay, sounds good.
[11:22] Samira: To close, let's recap action items. We'll: 1) Share integration spec and PoC checklist by 2025-03-18; 2) Runbook including metrics and security pack by the same date; 3) Nebula to share SKU list, traces, and compliance matrix by 2025-03-19/21. We'll coordinate calendars for a PoC scoping call week of 2025-03-24.
[11:50] Priya: That timeline works. Any other questions?
[11:56] Li: Just one — for the PoC, can we do a short cost model comparison? We want to see cost per 1M tokens across our SKUs vs Redwood's own hosted numbers.
[12:07] Samira: Yes, we'll run that and include assumptions in the perf spreadsheet.
[12:13] Alex: Great. Thanks all. We'll send notes and links; Samira will own the initial docs. Rafael will coordinate the dev contact.
[12:25] Priya: Thanks everyone. Looking forward to the next steps.
[12:30] (End of recorded segment — meeting continued with brief offline side-conversation about marketing assets)

Notes about transcription: occasional mishearing of proprietary names; some speaker attribution may be approximate.

Recap (from transcript):
- Objective: validate Redwood runtime on NebulaCloud GPUs, align on PoC scope (throughput + low-latency streaming), and surface marketplace integration options.
- Key technical points: SKUs are A100/H100 mixes; driver lock at host with containerized apps allowed; private control plane is supported; Prometheus metrics and KMS integrations available.
- Commercial: flexible revenue models (marketplace rev-share or direct billing), timeline for preview in Q2 possible.

References/Links mentioned in call: https://redwood.internal/papers/nebu-partner-onepager, https://sheets.example.com/redwood-nebula-benchmarks

End of transcript.
